17-13-0303-C(1) NARRATIVE ZONING ANALYSIS AND PLANS
APPLICANTS: CWP-ASR CHICAGO I LLC and CWP-ASR CHICAGO II LLC (as tenants in common)
SUBJECT PROPERTY: 201 East Walton Place, Chicago, Illinois
CURRENT ZONING: DX-7 Downtown Mixed-Use District
PROPOSED ZONING: DR-10 Downtown Residential District
LOT AREA: 21,709 square feet

PROJECT OVERVIEW:

The Property is a corner lot located on the South side of East Walton Place and the East side of North
Mies Van der Rohe Way, in the Streeterville neighborhood. The Property is currently improved with an
18-story building (plus basement), originally constructed in the 1950s as a residential condominium with
two hundred twenty-one (221) residential units, an interior parking garage for seventy-two (72) passenger
vehicles accessed by a curb cut and driveway on East Walton, ground floor commercial storefronts along
Walton, an interior loading area accessed by a curb-cut and driveway on North Mies Van der Rohe Way,
and limited outdoor space at ground level, also along Mies Van der Rose Way. One hundted and ten (110)
of the original condominiums were configured as what are now considered Efficiencies, and the other one
hundred and eleven (111) units are configured as standard dwelling units. The exterior configuration of the
Building envelope and the interior configuration of the 221 residential dwelling units, garage, and interior
loading area all remain, and the Applicants’ intention is to lease the property in its entirety as a residential
building with new amenities for the residential tenants. No commercial uses are proposed.

For various reasons, utilizing the Property for its original residential use requires rezoning the Property
pursuant to this requested Type 1 Map Amendment. Beginning in the 1980s, when the Property was zoned
RMB, the residential dwelling units were used for extended and short-term hotel stays pursuant to a Special
Use Approval from the City of Chicago Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA 185-88-S). The City also
downzoned the Property to DR-7 (in 2004), thereby reducing the Property’s maximum allowable residential
density and floor area ratio.l The City also adopted various text amendments following the Building’s
original construction that resulted in other Building conditions becoming non-conformities, including the
text amendment to require 36 square feet of on-site open space per dwelling unit and additional text
amendments modifying parking design requirements, loading requirements, and setback requirements.

CODE ANALYSIS AND REQUESTED RELIEF:

17-4-0200 Allowable Uses. The only proposed use of the Property will be Household Living, Multi-unit
(3-+units) residential above the ground floor, with residential amenities on the lower floors. These uses ate
all Permitted Uses under 17-4-0207 and do not require any Special Use approvals.

17-4-0300 General District Standards. This provision is inapplicable to the Property and project, as the
project does not involve new construction, and the Property is not within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA
rail station entrance or exit.

' Asa side note, a prior owner caused the site to be rezoned in 2016 from DR-7 to DX-7 to facilitate the
establishment of a Rosebud restaurant, but it appears that project did not come to fruition.

17-4-0400 Bulk and Density Standards.

17-4-0404 Lot Area per Unit. As noted above, Applicants are proposing to resume using the 221 existing
physical dwelling units for residential use and is not proposing to construct any new dwelling units.
That said, due to the prior downzoning, the requested Type 1 Map Amendment is necessary in order
for the Property to again have a Zoning District with an allowable residential density great enough for
the existing 221 units to be legally conforming.

Under DX-7 density limitations, the Property would have had to be at least 26,085 square feet in area.
[110 efficiencies x 90 sf/efficiency] + [111 dwelling units x 145 sf/dwelling unit] = 26,085 sf

Under DR-10 density limitations, the Property (which has a surveyed site area of 21,709 sf) will be legally
conforming again:
[110 efficiencies x 75 sf/efficiency] + [111 dwelling units x 115 sf/dwelling unit] = 21,015 sf

17-4-0405 Floor Area Ratio.
Under DX-7 FAR limitations, the Property would have a maximum FAR of 7.0.

The existing Floor Area of the Building, for Floor Area Ratio purposes, is approximately 169,053 square
feet, resulting in an existing Floor Area Ratio of approximately 7.8. (Please note that this Floor Area
calculation includes the existing Mechanical / Elevator Equipment Penthouse and Westerly Stair
enclosure but disregards approximately 10,000 - 11,000 square feet of area on the first floor of the
Building that is occupied by a portion of the on-site parking garage).

Under DR-10 density limitations, the Property will be legally conforming again, but Applicants are not
proposing to maximize available FAR through building additions. The only increases in the Propetty’s
FAR resulting from Applicants’ renovations would be technical increases (if any), arising from one or
both of the following: (i) the garage areas being added to Floor Area calculauons given parking relief
granted as part of the Type 1; and (i) Floor Area (if any) associated with adding a small rooftop
enclosure above the 19% Floor (shown and labeled “TBD” on the attached Plans). This rooftop
enclosure (if any) would house vertical circulation improvements for new rooftop decks and open
space, but its Floor Area impact is estimated to be between zero and 350 square feet, 42, an increase
of no more than 0.016%.

17-4-0406-A Front Setback.

The Property retains its original condition of having a zero (0) front setback. No front setback is required
in the DX District.

In the DR District, Buildings are subject to the R District front setback standards of 17-2-0305, Pursuant
to 17-2-0305-B, property owners may elect to have the front setback standard be the average front
yard depth existing on the nearest two lots on either side. However, given that the Property is a Corner
Lot, 17-2-0305-C dictates that the average setback be computed on the basis of the nearest two lots
that front on the same street as the subject lot. A recent survey performed by an Illinois licensed
architect (included with this Application) indicates that the average front setback for the buildings on
the neatest two lots that front on East Walton is 7.075 feet {(12.72 feet + 1.43feet)/2].

* Applicants are seeking 2 variation to reduce this required front setback from 7.075 feet to 0 feet, in
order to continue the existing condition. (Variation under Section 17-13-1101-B)

17-4-0406-B Side Setbacks.

Thete is no minimum side setback requirement in the DR district. (17-4-0406-B-2) The existing conditions
include a zero (0) setback on the East side of the Property and a 14.57-foot setback along the West
side of the Property (along Mies Van der Rohe Way).

17-4-0406-B Rear Setbacks.

The minimum rear setback for principal buildings other than detached houses in the DR District is 30%
of lot depth or 50 feet, whichever is less. The required rear setback for principal buildings other than
detached houses applies only to those portions of a building that are 18 feet or more above grade. (17-
4-0406-B-2) The Property is legally conforming with these requirements, as all floors above 14-feet in
height are set back 51.49 feet from the South property line.

17-4-0406-C Pedestrian Streets.

This Section is inapplicable to the Property and Project, as neither of the adjacent sights-of-way are
designated as Pedestrian Streets.

17-4-0407 Maximum Building Height and 17-4-0900 Planned Development Thresholds

‘There are no maximum building height limits in the “D” districts, however Planned Development review
and approval is required for buildings that exceed the building height thresholds established in 17-4-
0900 (and, by reference, in 17-8-0512-B). Pursuant to 17-8-0512-B, Residential Buildings in the
Downtown dash 10 District require Planned Development review if they meet or exceed 220 feet in
height. The existing building has a height that is below this threshold, and no additions to maximum
building height are proposed that would apply to this threshold. Specifically, as shown on the attached
Elevations, the building height is 162 feet when measuted in accordance with 17-17-0311-A (22, to the
underside of the top floor’s ceiling joist, given that the building has a flat roof).

‘As shown on the attached Elevations, the Rooftop currently includes an existing Mechanical / Elevator
Equipment Penthouse and an existing Westerly Stair enclosure, with uppermost limits of 182' -6" feet
above grade. The Elevations also depict one additional rooftop enclosure labeled “TBD”. This
enclosure would house new vertical circulation elements but would only be added if the renovations
include a new rooftop deck. Neither the rooftop deck nor the associated enclosure is being proposed
as mandatory project elements, since engineering, safety, usability, and cost considerations may
preclude their inclusion.

* As there is a possibility that neither the existing nor the proposed rooftop enclosures will meet all of the
height and setback criteria under 17-17-0311-B.1 and 17-17-0311-C, allowances for their inclusion in
Floor Area have been noted above, and Applicants are seeking relief to reduce the required setback for
the existing Westerly stairwell from 81' -8 */2" to 0, and, if necessary, to allow the uppermost height
of the rooftop enclosures to be 182’ 6”. (Pursuant to Optional Administrative Adjustments and Variations
under 17-13-0303-D, and Administrative Adjustwent under 17-13-1003-I (1.5) Other Setbacks and 17-13-
1003-L Building Height - General)

17-4-0408 Average Dwelling Unit Size.

The gross residential Floor Area developed on a Lot divided by the total aumber of dwelling units on such
